title: You killed one giant…
paragraphs:
You killed one giant…
but why does it feel like it came back?

You prayed.
You cried.
You thought it was over.

But here you are again—
fighting something that feels familiar.
Because no one told you this part:

And sometimes…
your greatest victory
is only the beginning of a deeper war.

Let me talk to the part of you
that’s tired of pretending.

You beat the addiction once.
Then it came back—quieter… smarter.

You walked away from that sin.
Then it returned—wearing a different name.

Ashamed.
Frustrated.
Questioning if your first victory even mattered.

“You didn’t really change.”
“You’re still the same person.”
“God must be tired of you by now.”

And slowly…
you start to believe it.

After Goliath fell…
there were still more giants.
“These four were descendants of Rapha in Gath, and they fell at the hands of David’s men.” (2 Samuel 21:22, NIV)

One had six fingers on each hand.
Another carried a spear like Goliath’s.
Some scholars interpret these giants as literal descendants of a clan of warriors from Gath—physically imposing enemies of Israel.
Sin doesn’t always die in one blow.

You thought lust was gone—
then it came back as fantasy.

You thought pride was buried—
then it rose as insecurity.

You thought anger was healed—
then it returned as silence and withdrawal.
And this is where shame tries to bury you alive.

Because you expected instant perfection.
But God is working through a process.

You wanted one battle.
But this is a war.
David didn’t kill all the giants.
“They fell at the hands of David’s men.” (2 Samuel 21:22)
But he didn’t finish it alone.
This destroys the lie that says:
“If I were stronger, I wouldn’t need help.”
God never designed you to fight alone.

Some giants fall
only when you stop hiding.
Only when you bring someone into the battle.
“Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed.”
Why does it hurt so much when the giant comes back?
Because you thought your past was buried.

But now it feels like proof…
that you never changed.

Because your identity is not defined
by recurring battles.

It’s defined
by the finished work of Jesus Christ.

Every giant—
sin, shame, addiction, pride, fear—
did not just get wounded there.
“He forgave us all our sins, having canceled the charge of our legal indebtedness… He has taken it away, nailing it to the cross.”

Your salvation is complete.
Your transformation is ongoing.

You are saved instantly.
But you are healed progressively.
That’s why the giants feel like they come back.
But because God is forming you.
Teaching you to fight with Him, not without Him.
And here’s the Gospel truth you need to hear:
You are not fighting for victory.

The debt is paid.
The power of sin is broken.
The enemy is defeated.
So why does the battle still feel real?
Because the enemy wants you to forget what’s already been won.
“For though the righteous fall seven times, they rise again…”
Because righteousness is not about never falling.

Some of you are stuck
not because you’re weak—
“I’ll fix this first… then I’ll come back.”
“Come as you are. I’ll fix you.”
But turning your heart back to Him.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just and will forgive us… and purify us from all unrighteousness.”
So why are you still hiding?
Your giant grows stronger in the dark.
But it weakens in the light.

Not to pretend.
Not to perform.
Because Jesus is not waiting to condemn you.
“There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.”
Yes—even the thing you’re thinking about right now.
Or will you surrender the battle to the One who already won?
But your Savior has already defeated them all.
What is the “other giant” in your life right now?
The one you didn’t expect to face again?

“Lord Jesus, I’m tired of fighting alone.
I confess my sin. I turn back to You.
Break every chain. Heal every hidden place.
I receive Your grace. I trust Your cross.
Teach me to walk in victory. Amen.”
